newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 20.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Senior officials of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation have agreed on how to reach their goal of eliminating trade and ivnestment barriers, an official says. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- Seven back-up planes, including the biggest U.S. military aircraft, the C-5 Galaxy Star Lifter, will beef up the security measures for U.S. President Bill Clinton when he arrives for the APEC meetings in Manila and Subic. (INQUIRER)
- President Fidel Ramos pushes for a still unnamed successor who will assure the continuity and durability of his reforms. (MANILA TIMES)
- The opening of the APEC friendship lane slows down traffic to a crawl in Manila's main roads (CHRONICLE)

- The Philipine economy is expected to grow by 7.16 percent in the first nine months of the year compared with a 5.6 percent GNP growth in the same period last year, the average from a Reuter poll of analysts show (INQUIRER)
- The local banking system's total investments in the real estate sector are well within acceptable levels, the Central Bank says. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- About $2 billion in bilateral investments agreements are expected to be signed after the APEC meeting, trade and industry secretary Cesar Bautista says (BUSINESS TIMES)
